FMA No. 114 of 2013,/ FMAT No.614 of 2012
With 
Civil Rule No. 647(FM)/2012
lawyer:
Subrata Chowdhury with Reshma Sultana, Advocates -----For the Appellants.
Md Kamrul Alam, Advocate -----For the Respondent No.1. 
Md Fakhar Uddin, Advocate -----For the Respondent No.2.
parties:
A Hakim Gazi and others ------ Plaintiff Appellants
Vs.
Md Nasiruddin, Assistant Vice President/Manager and others ------ Defendant Respondents
full_judgment:
2. In the instant First Miscellaneous Appeal (FMA), the plaintiff as appellant has challenged the judgment and order dated 28-3-2012 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Chandpur in Title Suit No. 20 of 2012 by which the ad-interim order of injunction passed on 8-3- 2012 has been vacated. 

 3. Be it stated that during pendency of the instant FMA, the original plaintiff-appellant namely Abdul Hakim Gazi died on 1-1-2014. Thereafter, his wife, son and 3 daughters, who are his legal heirs, have been substituted in place of the deceased plaintiff-appellant by order dated 23-2-2014. One of the legal heirs of the deceased plaintiff namely Md Humayun Kabir Gazi, who was the proforma defendant No.3 in the original suit and also proforma opposite party No.3 in this FMA has been substituted as appellant No. 1 (b). 

 4. The case of the plaintiff, as averred in the plaint, in short, is that his son Md Humayun Kabir Gazi in 2003, obtained investment facility of Taka 1,00,000 for business purposes for his business enterprise M/s Sabbir Gazi Furniture from Islami Bank Bangladesh Limited, Chandpur branch as per sanction advice issued by the defendant No.1 (Manager Islami Bank Limited Bangladesh, Chandpur branch). Against the said sanction advice the plaintiff, as guarantor of the loan, mortgaged the (Ka) scheduled property owned by him comprising of 0.31 decimals of land and structures constructed thereon situated in Chandpur district by executing and registering a mortgage deed being No. 4923 on 7-10-2003 in favour of the bank. On the same day the plaintiff also executed and registered an irrevocable power of attorney being No. 4924 in favour of the bank. The plaintiff's son repaid the said investment facility with profit. On 22-1-2012 the plaintiff received a notice from Assistant Commissioner (Land), Chandpur Sadar and thereafter on inquiry he came to know that on 12-10-2011 the bank published an auction notice in the newspaper for sale of the (Ka) scheduled property on the ground that his son had defaulted in repaying the bank loan and on 9-1-2012 the bank executed and registered a sale deed being No.158 in respect of the said property in favour of the auction purchaser namely Chandpur Multipurpose Cooperative Society Ltd., Chandpur (defendant No.2). 

 5. Challenging the auction notice dated 12-10-2011, auction held on 26-10-2011 and registered sale deed No. 158 dated 9-1-2012 and also praying for a permanent injunction restraining the defendants from evicting the plaintiff from the (Ka) scheduled property or transferring the same, the plaintiff instituted the suit. 

 6. The plaintiff filed the suit on 8-3-2012 and on the same day filed an application for temporary injunction against the defendants. The court below vide order dated 8-3-2012 passed an ad-interim injunction restraining the defendants from evicting the plaintiff from the scheduled property or transferring the same till submission of written objection by the defendants and hearing of the same. 

 7. The defendants contested the injunction application by filing separate written objections on 27-3-2012. In the instant FMA, the written objection filed by the defendant No.1 i.e., the bank, has been produced before us by the plaintiff-appellant and although the FMA has been contested by both the defendants, the written objection filed by the defendant No. 2 has not been filed. 

 8. The case of the defendant No. 1, as stated in the written objection, is that the suit is not maintainable and barred by the principles of estoppel, waiver and acquiescence. The specific case of the defendant No.1 bank is that in 2003 the plaintiff's son obtained investment facility of Taka 1,00,000 as per sanction advice No. IBBL/CHAND/03 dated 4-10-2003. Against the said investment facility the plaintiff on 7-10-2003 executed and registered mortgage deed No.4923 and a deed of irrevocable power of attorney No.4924 in favour of the bank. Subsequently, upon prayer of the plaintiff's son the said investment facility was enhanced to Taka 4,00,000. Thereafter, vide another sanction advice dated 10-8-2009 the said investment facility was enhanced to Taka 8,00,000 and against the said additional investment facility the plaintiff on 9-9-2009 executed a deed of agreement and deposited the same with the bank. The plaintiff's- son availed investment facility of Taka 8,00,000 from the bank but defaulted in repaying the 'same within the stipulated period, The bank sent a legal notice under section 12 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 to the plaintiff's son who received the same on 17-8-2011, but did not repay the loan. Thereafter, under the provisions of section 12 of the Ain, the bank on 12-10-2011 published auction notices in the national Daily Sangram newspaper and in a local newspaper called Daily Chandpur Diganta. In response to the said auction notice the defendant No. 2 and two others submitted auction bids. Auction was held on 26-10-2011. The defendant No. 2 became the highest bidder which is Taka 65,41,000. On 9-1-2012 the bank executed and registered the sale deed No.158 in respect of the mortgaged property in favour of defendant. No.2. Out of the sale proceeds the bank adjusted its out- standing dues of Taka 10,29,359.74 and paid the rest amount of Taka 55,11,640.22 to the plaintiff in cash which was received. and acknowledged by the plaintiff. 

 9. After hearing the parties the court below vide the impugned judgment and order dated 28-3-2012 vacated the earlier order of ad-interim injunction dated 8-3-2012. Challenging the order dated 28-3-2012 the plaintiff preferred the instant FMA before this Court which has been admitted on 30-7-2012. 

 11. Mr Subrata Chowdhury, the learned Advocate appearing for the plaintiff-appellants, submits that at the time of the auction sale the market price of the (Ka) scheduled property was about Taka 6 crore, but in connivance between the defendants the same was sold at a shockingly low price at Taka 65,41,000 which amounts to fraud. He next submits the borrower i.e., the original plaintiff's son repaid the loan taken- in 2003 against which the plaintiff mortgaged the property and gave the power to the bank to sell the property in case of default by his son, but the bank fraudulently published the auction notice in 2011 for sale of the plaintiffs, mortgaged property for alleged non-payment, of the loan taken in 2009 and hence the auction sale is illegal and not binding upon the plaintiff. 

 12. Mr Chowdhury draws our attention to the power of attorney no. 4924 dated 7-10-2003 and the registered sale deed No. 158 dated 9-1-2012 (Annexure- X2 and Z respectively of the supplementary affidavit dated 22-10-2014 filed by the plaintiff-appellants) by which the bank transferred the property as attorney of the plaintiff (since deceased) to the auction purchaser (defendant No. 2) and submits that the bank had no legal right to sell the property on the basis of the said power of attorney inasmuch has the power of attorney ceased to be operative and became invalid for subsequent loan facility availed by the plaintiff's son in 2009 for which the plaintiff was neither a guarantor nor executed any power of attorney and since the bank had no legal right to sell the property both the auction notice and sale of the property to the defendant No.2 are void ab initio. He submits that the plaintiff-appellants have a good prima facie arguable case. "He submits that the substituted legal heirs of the deceased plaintiff reside at the (Ka) scheduled property and the building constructed thereon and as such the balance of convenience and inconvenience are in favour of the plaintiff-appellants and if an order of injunction is not granted the plaintiff-appellants would suffer irreparable loss and-injury which cannot be compensated in money. 

 13. On the other hand, Mr Md Kamrul Alam, the learned Advocate for the defendant-respondent No.1 bank, submits that following the auction sale, the bank, after deducting its outstanding liability, returned the balance amount to the plain- tiff which he received in cash and thus accepted and acknowledged the auction notice and auction sale and now he is estopped from denying the same. He submits that the plaintiff cannot approbate and reprobate at the same time. The learned advocate draws .our attention to memo No. 00. 293.027.08.27.010.2012-332 dated 4-4-2012 signed by the Executive Magistrate and Surveyor, Revenue Section, both of the office of Deputy Commissioner, Chandpur (Annexure-X series of the supplementary affidavit dated 27-10-2014 filed by the respondent No.1) by which the possession of the auction sold property was handed over to the defendant No.2. The learned advocate also refers to order dated 5-4-2012 passed by the court below in which the learned court referred to the submission of the learned advocate of the plaintiff that after vacating the order of injunction the defendants forcibly took possession of the property. 

 14. Mr Md Kamrul Alam submits that since the plaintiff received the sale proceeds and possession of the property has been handed over to defendant No.2 on 4-4-2012 prior to filing of the instant FMA, the same has become infructuous and order of injunction as prayed for by the appellants cannot be granted. 

 15. The learned Advocate then refers to section 12(8) of the Ain, 2003 and submits that in case of auction sale held illegally or with irregularity, the same cannot be challenged. However, the owner of the mortgaged property may sue the bank for any loss, if suffered because of such illegal or irregular auction sale or for sale the property at a shockingly low price as alleged by the plaintiff. In support of the argument the learned Advocate relies upon the case of Banesa Bibi vs Senior Vice President 8 LG (2011) AD 55 = 63 DLR (AD) 160. 

 16. Rebutting the argument of the learned Advocate of the plaintiff-appellants in respect of the bank's having no legal right to sell, Mr Alam the learned Advocate for the respondent No. 1 bank, submits that the guarantee given by the plaintiff against the loan taken by his son in 2003 is a continuing guarantee and as such the bank had the legal right to sell the property. The learned Advocate further submits that the plaintiff does not have any prima facie arguable case and since the application for injunction has become infructuous the instant FMA is liable to be dismissed. 

 17. In reply, Mr Chowdhury, the learned Advocate for the appellants, submits that so far as handing over of the possession of the property is concerned, the plaintiff-appellants are still in possession of the property and memo dated 4-4-2012 referred to by the learned Advocate for the bank is merely a paper transaction which was never acted upon. 

 21. Admittedly, the plaintiff's son obtained investment facility of Taka 1,00,000 from the bank as per sanction advice dated 4-10-2003. Against the said loan, the plaintiff, as guarantor of the same, mortgaged the property by executing and registering a mortgage deed and the power of attorney on 7-10-2003 in favour of the bank. In the written statement filed by the bank it has been stated that the said loan was enhanced to Taka 4,00,000. Thereafter, vide another sanction advice dated 13-8-2009 (Annexure Z-3 of the supplementary affidavit dated 8-12-2014 filed by the respondent No.1) the existing loan was renewed and enhanced to Taka 8,00,000 which the plaintiff's son availed in full. 

 22. In the written statement filed by the bank it has further been stated that against the enhanced loan the plaintiff on 9-9-2009 executed a deed of agreement on Taka 150 stamped papers and deposited the same with the bank(মোঃ হুমাযুন কবির গাজীর অনুরোধে তাহার পিতা বিগত ৯-৯-২০০৯ইং তারিখে ১৫০ টাকার স্ট্যাপে বদ্ধকের অতিরিক্ত ৭,০০,০০০বিনিয়োগের (ঋণের) জন্য বদ্ধকের অতিরিক্ত বিনিয়োগের (ঋণের) অতিরিক্ত চুক্তিপত্র দলিল সম্পাদন করিয়া ব্যাংকে জমা প্রদান করিলে......). This document has not been produced before us. It appears that against the enhanced loan of Taka 8,00,000 the plaintiff neither executed any mortgage deed nor power of attorney. 

 23. In the legal notice dated 17-8-2011 given by the bank to the plaintiff's son, copy of which was given to the plaintiff (Annexure-Y of the supplementary affidavit dated 26-11-2013 filed the respondent No.1) it has been stated that between the period from 17-9-2009 to 9-6-2010 the plaintiff’s son availed investment facility of total Taka 8,00,000 in 10 installments, but he defaulted in repaying the same with profit. 

 24. The bank published auction notices in daily and local newspapers on 12-10-2011. The auction sale was held on 26-10-2011 in which the defendant No.2 became the highest bidder. On 9-1-2012 the bank executed and registered the sale deed No. 158 in respect of the mortgaged property to the defendant No.2 as attorney of the plaintiff by dint of registered power of attorney No. 4924 dated 7-10-2003. 

 28. The learned Advocate for the appellants submits that if the bank has no legal power to sell the mortgaged property or has not been given the power to sell the same, all the subsequent actions taken by the bank including publication of auction notice, the auction sale and transfer of the property to the auction purchaser becomes void ab initio. On the other hand, the learned Advocates for the respondents submit that section 12(8) of the Ain and the proviso thereof gives statutory protection to both the bank and the auction purchaser in respect of any illegality or irregularity committed in the process of the auction sale and inspite of such illegality or irregularity the auction purchaser acquires valid title. The remedy open to the owner of the mortgaged property is to file a suit for compensation and as such the instant suit not being maintainable, the plaintiff does not have prima facie arguable case. 

 32. In the facts and circumstances of the case, as discussed above, now, the question before us for consideration is whether the bank had the legal right to seel the mortgaged property of the plaintiff as his attorney under the power of attorney dated 7-10-2003 executed against the loan taken by his son in 2003 for defaulting in repaying of the loan availed by his son in 2009-2010 as per sanction advice dated 13-8-2009 for which the plaintiff was neither a guarantor nor executed any power of attorney. It appears that this point was not raised before the court below and consequently, the same was not discussed. 

 33. The learned Advocate for the bank respondent No.1 draws our attention to both the registered mortgage deed No. 4923 dated 7-10-2003 executed by the plaintiff in favour of the bank as guarantor for his son's loan and the power of attorney No. 4924 dated 7-10-2003 and submits that the guarantee in question is a continuing guarantee and the loan taken in 2003 has been merged in the renewed and enhanced loan taken in 2009-2010 and therefore, the bank had the 'legal right to sell' the property. 

 35. In the instant case, whether the loan taken in 2003 has been merged in the renewed and enhanced loan taken in 2009-2010, the guarantee given by the plaintiff in 2003 is a continuing guarantee and thus under section 12 of the Ain, 2003 the bank had the legal right to sell the mortgaged property as attorney of the plaintiff under the power of attorney dated 7-10-2003 which was executed against the loan taken in 2003 are to be determined by the trial Court upon taking evidence and scrutinising the terms of the relevant documents and transactions entered into between the parties. The instant case relates to an interlocutory matter of injunction. Therefore, we are not in a position to determine the issue without taking evidence. However, considering the facts and circumstances discussed above, we find a prima facie arguable case in favour of the plaintiff-appellants on this point. 

 36. So far as the other principles governing the law of injunction i.e., the balance of convenience and inconvenience and irreparable loss are concerned, we note that the plaintiff received the sale proceeds of the auction sale from the bank. It is the case of the bank that according to the provisions of section 12 of the Ain, 2003 it took over the possession of the property on 4-4-2012 and handed over the same to the auction purchaser, which is evident from memo dated 4-4-2012 signed by the Executive Magistrate and Surveyor, Revenue Section, both of the office of Deputy Commissioner, Chandpur but the same has been denied by the appellants and their case is that the said memo is a paper transaction and was not acted upon. The appellants are still in possession of the suit property. 

 37. In the supplementary affidavit filed on behalf of the defendant No.2 auctioneer purchaser, it has been stated that the auction purchaser has been possessing the suit land and constructed a boundary wall surrounding the same. However, they did not file any document supporting the claim as to possession, So, we find a prima facie case in favour of the plaintiff-appellants in respect of the possession of the suit property. 

 38. Since we have already found a prima facie arguable case in favour of the plaintiff, it is our considered view that justice would be served by passing an order of status quo in respect of possession and position of the suit property in question.
